newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh unveils $46 billion five-year plan.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh unveils $46 billion five-year plan.

text.p: Bangladesh, where nearly half of the population lives in poverty, said on Saturday it would spend around 2,034 billion taka ($46.2 billion) in the next five years to spur economic growth by an annual average of more than seven percent.
A newly-released draft five-year plan said 21 percent of the funding would come from overseas aid, with the aim of attracting more than 50 percent from the private sector.
"It's a matter of shame for Bangladesh to step into the coming century with so much poverty," Foreign Minister Abdus Samad Azad told a national seminar debating the plan.
Azad said the plan was designed to fight poverty and face the challenges of the 21st century.
"We must have specific programmes that will generate employment and reduce the poverty level," he said.

The 1997-2002 plan is three times bigger than the previous one. It envisages gross domestic product growth of 6.01 percent in 1997/98, 7.27 in 1998/99, 7.55 in 1999/2000, 7.98 in 2000/2001 and 8.54 percent in 2001/2002.
Azad said Bangladesh had failed to make the desired progress in reducing poverty despite its attempts at socio-economic development.
"The policymakers and implementing agencies must find out the reasons for the slower impact of such plans on the country's poverty situation," he said.
The plan aims to reduce the "below poverty line" population to 30 percent from 45 percent now, and to raise per capita income by an annual rate of six percent.
It also envisages curbing population growth to 1.36 percent from around two percent at present. It foresees the country's population swelling to 132.5 million in 2002 from the present 123.8 million.
The draft said population growth would be contained through raising the rate of contraceptive use to 60 percent at the end of the plan period from the current 48 percent.
The country's literacy rate will be increased to 75 percent from the present 47.3, the plan predicts.
Bangladesh's food production, mainly rice, is expected to rise to 25.12 million tonnes by the end of the plan period from the present 20.39 million. ($ = 44 Bangladesh Taka)
